title: Real Madrid’s Antonio Rudiger in talks over contract extension
content:
Antonio Rudiger, the Germany international defender, is in talks over an extended contract with Real Madrid.

The 33-year-old’s current deal expires at the end of this season and, without an extension, he would become a free agent in the summer.

The parties are yet to come to an agreement and discussions are set to continue, with the expectation that a resolution either way could be reached next week.

Sources from the dressing room, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said the squad expects Rudiger to continue at Madrid next season, when Jose Mourinho is poised to return to the Bernabeu as head coach.

Madrid have a policy of offering players over 30 only a one-year extension, so should he agree a new deal, Rudiger is likely to be tied to the club until summer 2027.

Rudiger’s season has been disrupted by injuries to his hamstring and knee, restricting him to just 18 appearances in La Liga and seven in the Champions League – as Madrid finished without silverware for a second consecutive campaign.

Rudiger joined Madrid from Chelsea ahead of the 2022-23 season and has made 182 appearances since, winning eight trophies including La Liga and the Champions League in 2023-24.

He played 50 games in all competitions last year during a campaign in which Madrid struggled again with defensive options as they tried to defend their league title, finishing second and four points off champions Barcelona.

Rudiger has made 82 senior appearances for Germany and is expected to be named in their squad for this summer’s World Cup.

Analysis by Real Madrid correspondent Mario Cortegana

Madrid had intended to have this case resolved some time ago and it is considered a key decision in the making of next season’s squad.

Even if Rudiger has had some avoidable moments, the German is highlighted internally as one of the few leaders in a dressing room in desperate need of authority. Dean Huijsen or Endrick are two of the young players who can attest to the positive impact of his seniority, with the Brazilian saying as much in January 2025.

On a footballing level, Rudiger’s prime can be considered to have passed, largely because he sacrificed himself for the needs of the team. The 33-year-old spent months last season taking painkillers even for training. And yet his contribution for a fair number of games will surely be important next season.

The financial aspect should not be forgotten either. With David Alaba set to leave the club as free agent after not having a renewal offer, Eder Militao continually hit by injuries or Raul Asencio’s dip in form, the club is planning to reinforce the position. Rudiger’s departure would lead to the need for a major investment at a time when Madrid are looking to strengthen the squad while at the same time maintaining a healthy balance sheet.
